title: Performance attestations: onboarding, version-locking, and automated refresh hooks for model profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and ship a repeatable, auditable way to publish Redwood-verified performance profiles as signed 'performance attestations' that can be pinned to model versions and runtime bundles, and which support automated refresh hooks for drift detection. These attestations will encode latency/throughput/cost baselines for a model under canonical load shapes and hardware configurations, include a signature for provenance, and expose metadata useful for routing/fallback decisions in the serving layer. This ticket covers the publishing schema, authoring UX/API, pinning semantics, refresh cadence, and an initial automated benchmark workflow that produces attestations and writes audit records to the catalog.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New performance attestation JSON schema is approved and documented with required fields (model_id, model_version, runtime_bundle_hash, benchmark_config, latency_p50/p95, throughput_ops/sec, cost_per_1k_tokens, signature, published_by, published_at, ttl_or_refresh_policy).
A2: Console and API surfaces exist to create a new attestation, with an option to pin customer-facing model aliases to a specific model_version + runtime_bundle_hash combo.

A3: Automated benchmark pipeline (GitHub Actions → benchmark cluster) runs for a sample model and produces a signed attestation, stores it in the profile catalog, and emits an audit log entry and a Console notification on success/failure.

A4: Runtime can consume attestations and make routing decisions; a canary flow uses attestation metadata to prefer pinned variants and fall back to compatible variants when pinned variant is unhealthy.
A5: Rollback flow: Console allows un-pinning and reverting to previous attestation; this action creates an audit record and triggers an optional re-benchmark job.
A6: Security controls: attestation signing keys are KMS-backed; only authorized roles can publish attestations; publishing events are logged for compliance.
A7: Documentation and an operational runbook for stale attestations (TTL expiry, refresh failure handling) are published in Confluence and linked from the Console.
A8: Cost vs cadence tradeoffs documented: baseline recommended refresh cadence (monthly) and guidelines for high-change models to use weekly refresh.
notes: Design trade-off: include full sample distributions vs only p50/p95. Engineering prefers compact attestation (p50/p95 + histogram hash) to limit storage and signing cost.
Bench infra costs: running a full throughput matrix across instance types is expensive; prototype will run canonical shapes (short chat, long form, embeddings) and a limited set of instance sizes.
Security note: use KMS asymmetric keys for signing to avoid storing private keys on CI runners. Work with Security to rotate keys quarterly.
UX: Console should show 'staleness' badge when attestation is older than recommended TTL and offer one-click re-benchmark with dry-run mode.
Observability: attach benchmark run GitHub Actions logs and perf graphs to the attestation record in the catalog for quick triage.
We should avoid exposing raw cost-per-token estimates for private deployments; instead surface relative cost tiers and allow customers to opt-in to concrete numbers.
updates: 2025-01-17: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Diego, Mei Chen), Security (Liam O'Connor), and Design (Sofia Martins). Agreed schema required fields and KMS signing approach.
2025-01-22: Engineering proposed compact schema and histogram-hash approach to reduce attestation size (ENG-4012). Decision: include p50/p95 + sample_histogram_hash.
2025-01-28: Design provided Console flows for publishing and pinning. Feedback: emphasize audit trail and rollback affordances.
2025-01-31: Prototype GH Action for benchmark pipeline submitted (PR #312). Initial run succeeded for sample-model-x with p50/p95 values recorded.
2025-02-02: Security review requested; KMS key policy draft under review by Liam. Next: add integration tests for signature verification in the catalog service.
final_decision_or_solution: Adopt compact attestation schema (p50/p95 + histogram hash), sign with KMS-managed RSA key, implement publishing API + Console UI for authoring and pinning, and ship an automated benchmark pipeline that writes attestations to the catalog and emits audit events. Default refresh cadence set to 30 days with override options and an on-demand re-benchmark button.
implementation_notes: API: POST /attestations to publish; GET /attestations?model_id=&version= to list; PUT to update TTL or pin metadata.
Catalog storage: store attestation JSON in S3 + metadata in Postgres. Keep raw benchmark artifacts in a separate bucket with lifecycle rules.
Runtime changes: add attestation consumer to routing layer with simple pin check and fallback policy on health degradation.
Bench pipeline: containerized benchmark runner, GH Action triggers container on dedicated infra. Action returns signed attestation via KMS-assisted signing service.
Compliance: bind publishing permission to role 'attestation_publisher' and require MFA for production key usage.
